explanation: The I47V mutation reduces a critical hydrophobic contact point in the flap region by removing ~27 Ų of buried surface area, weakening van der Waals interactions between isoleucine's larger branched side chain and lopinavir's binding surface at the 2.2 Å interface. This volumetric loss slightly diminishes the favorable hydrophobic complementarity that stabilizes the inhibitor-protease complex, resulting in marginally weaker binding affinity. Although the energetic cost is modest (~0.1 kcal/mol), the reduction in optimal packing geometry within this critical flap-contact region provides a mechanistic basis for partial resistance that accumulates when combined with other mutations.
